summary: Bradford's transit positions span TTC reliability and safety, transit expansion (especially in Scarborough), congestion and gridlock, active transportation, and ride-share. Bradford supports a 15-minute TTC money-back guarantee, platform edge doors, uniformed police at every subway station, and station cleanliness/lighting standards. Bradford backs the Eglinton East and Scarborough LRTs, opposes what he calls Scarborough being left behind on funding, and supports building rapid transit separated from traffic. On gridlock, Bradford has called for a Congestion Relief Commissioner, opposed the RapidTO permanent reconfiguration, opposed Bloor West bike lanes while supporting Danforth bike lanes built with consultation, and proposed temporarily reopening King Street to vehicles. Bradford opposes the rideshare cap, supports Bike Share expansion, electric buses, fare freezes, and the Fair Pass program. Bradford has consistently framed transit and traffic as core city responsibilities requiring accountability.

key_positions.stance: Supports a 15-minute TTC money-back guarantee that refunds fares when service is delayed by 15 minutes or more, modeled on GO Transit, London, Singapore, and Washington DC.
Supports a TTC safety package: uniformed police at every subway station, cleanliness and lighting standards, and platform edge doors system-wide.
Supports expanding transit in Scarborough, including the Eglinton East LRT and Scarborough LRT, and characterizes current funding as leaving Scarborough behind.
Supports building rapid transit separated from car traffic, citing Finch West as an example where road-sharing produced delays.
Supports creating a Congestion Relief Commissioner / Traffic Czar with responsibility and accountability for Toronto traffic.
Opposes the proposed cap on Uber and Lyft vehicles, stating it raises prices, lengthens waits, and reduces service in underserved areas.
Supports bike lanes built case-by-case with community consultation; supports the Danforth bike lane process and opposes how Bloor West was implemented.
Opposes the RapidTO permanent reconfiguration of Bathurst and Dufferin, proposing a time-limited World Cup pilot following the 2015 Pan Am model.
Supports temporarily reopening King Street to vehicles while streetcars are diverted due to construction.
Supports Bike Share Toronto expansion, electric buses, accessible stations, and TTC fare freezes; supports the Fair Pass program.
Opposes tearing down the Gardiner Expressway, characterizing it as keeping drivers in gridlock.
States Toronto is the most congested city in North America and that traffic/congestion is the top issue residents raise.
